title: Peter Naur's "Programming as Theory Building" (1985)
explainer: Computer scientist Peter Naur argued in a 1985 essay that the real "program" is a theory of the problem and its solution that lives in the programmers' heads, and that source code and documentation alone cannot fully transfer that theory to someone new. His case studies, including a team that could extend a program smoothly while another team with the same code and documents could not, speak directly to why reading someone else's codebase is a harder and different skill than reading code you wrote yourself.
